payload.sectionRef: § 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and

paragraphs.text: 1.4 HDI shall provide the Company with access to, and

the right to use, a computer system on which the Site will be stored and operated, with a direct Internet connection of shared but greater than T-1 bandwidth, plus capacity to process continuously during burst periods. HDI shall also provide the Company with access to HDI's software and Content administration tools for purposes of allowing the Company to monitor current catalog information.

1.5 For the purposes of collecting orders for Deerskin Products from the Site and to communicate to the Site the unavailability of certain Deerskin Products, HDI shall provide export files in the format provided by the Company. HDI shall bear the programming and software costs relating to efforts required to create order export files and receive and process import files of the Company's inventory information.

1.6 HDI shall have the Site fully operational and accessible on demand by users of the Internet no later than sixty (60) days from the date this Agreement has been executed by both Parties. In the event that HDI fails to have the Site fully operational within seventy (70) days from the date of this Agreement, the Company shall have the right to terminate this Agreement without penalty.
1.7 HDI shall distribute the Site through the world wide protocol of the Internet using distribution channels used by HDI sites and other similar distribution channels.
1.8 HDI agrees that it shall promote the Site and Deerskin Products no less favorably than it promotes HDI's

catalog titles. HDI's promotion of the Site and Deerskin Products shall include, but not be limited to, the incorporation of the Site and Deerskin Products into HDI's promotion calendars with Xoom.com and Excite for the term of this Agreement. HDI agrees that the costs of any such promotions shall be borne by HDI.
2. Company's Responsibilities.
2.1 The Company shall provide all Content to HDI to be included in the Site no later than ten (10) days from the date this Agreement has been executed by both Parties.
2.2 The Company shall bear all costs associated with the processing of customer orders.
3. Fees; Payment.

3.1 The Company shall pay HDI thirty percent (3016) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month. "Net Sales" shall mean all revenues from the sale of Deerskin Products on the Site including shipping and handling charges, minus refunds and exchanges.
3.2 Payments to HDI shall be due monthly within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar month and shall be accompanied by documentation reasonably detailing the calculation of the payment.

3.3 Quarterly reconciliation of payments shall be conducted within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar quarter to adjust for refunds and exchanges not taken into account in payments made to HDI.

3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
4. Term; Termination; Termination Payment.

4.1 Term; Termination. This Agreement shall be effective as of that date (the "Effective Date") the Site becomes fully operational as set forth in writing and executed by both Parties and shall continue for a period of one (1) year from the Effective Date. This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
4.2 Termination Payment.

(a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
(b) In the event that the amount of the Termination

Payment is determined pursuant to this Section 4.2 to be less than or equal to zero, then no Termination Payment shall be due to HDI nor shall HDI be required to make any termination payment to the Company if the amount is determined to be less than zero.
(c) The Termination Payment, if any, shall be payable by the Company in eight (8) equal payments to be made quarterly, commencing thirty (30) days after the termination date.
5. Site; Site Management.

5.1 URL. The Uniform Resource Locator, or address on the World Wide Web for the Site ("URL") shall be as mutually agreed by the Parties and shall be established and registered as necessary by HDI at no cost to the Company.

5.2 The Company shall have exclusive artistic and editorial control over the Site, including, without limitation, the implementation of the Content on the Site and the design and look and feel of the Site. Neither the Site nor any portion of thereof shall be deemed accepted and approved by the Company unless and until the Company accepts and approves same in writing to HDI. No portion of the Site shall be made available on the Internet without the consent of the Company.

5.3 The Company shall be deemed the "merchant of record" for all commercial transactions on the Site related to Deerskin Products. Until the sale of the Deerskin Products to the consumer from the Site all title to the Deerskin Products shall remain with the Company.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

paragraphs.text: 5.4 Each of HDI and the Company shall appoint a

General Manager of its own to act as liaison with the other Party for the Site (each a "General Manager") who shall bear sole responsibility for bookkeeping and business operations of the Site on a day-today basis. Each General Manager shall have the authority to make and convey decisions on behalf of each Party and to be the liaison with the other Party for all production and Content matters.
6. Exclusivity.

6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
The Company hereby grants to HDI a non-exclusive, limited, non-transferable license to use the Company's "Deerskin" trademarks, service

marks, and logos (collectively, "Marks") solely for the purpose of carrying out its obligations under this Agreement. Except as provided herein, no licenses of the Company's Marks are granted or implied under this Agreement.
6.2 The Company retains the right to establish a web site on the Internet for the purpose of offering closeout
merchandise which may be identified as "Deerskin" branded products, if such is the case.

6.3 During the term of this Agreement and for a period of two years after the expiration date of this Agreement, HDI shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet from which products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) are offered for sale to consumers on the Internet.
7. Cross-Promotions.

7.1 Joint Efforts. The Parties agree to cross-promote one another's products through the use of their respective customer e-mail lists on a reciprocal and equitable basis. The Parties specifically agree that the form, content and design of any and all advertisements or promotional materials featuring the other Party or such Party's products shall continue to be developed by or on behalf of such Party and shall be subject to such Party's final approval. The Parties agree further that any promotions or advertisements involving the use of a Party's customer e-mail list by the other Party shall be subject to the prior approval of such Party.

7.2 Mutual Covenants as to Advertisements. The Parties hereby covenant and agree that their respective marketing and advertising efforts provided for herein shall at all times comply with all applicable laws rules and regulations and will

not contain any material which is obscene, threatening, fraudulent, harassing, libelous, infringing of third party intellectual property rights, otherwise illegal or, in the reasonable judgment of the Party required to display or transmit the advertisement, offensive.
8. Confidentiality.

8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by the Company, HDI shall maintain the strict confidentiality and shall not disclose to any third party the existence of, or terms and conditions of this Agreement. In addition, HDI, in performing the Services for the Company hereunder, may have access to or be exposed to, directly or indirectly, Content, user information, data, knowledge and proprietary and trade secret information of the Company in oral, graphic, written, electronic or machine readable form (hereinafter collectively referred to as "Confidential Information"). Confidential Information shall not include information which can be demonstrated:
(a) to have been rightfully in the possession of HDI from a source other than the Company prior to the time of disclosure of said information to HDI hereunder ("Time of Receipt");
(b) to have been in the public domain prior to the Time of Receipt;

(c) to have become part of the public domain after the Time of Receipt by a publication or by any other means except an unauthorized act or omission or breach of this Agreement on the part of HDI, its employees, or agents; or (d) to have been supplied to HDI after the Time of Receipt by a third party who is under no obligation to the
Company to maintain such information in confidence.

8.2 HDI Obligations. All Confidential Information of the Company shall be held in strict confidence by HDI and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of the Company, except as may be required by law. HDI shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for Confidential Information, including measures at least as strict as those HDI uses to protect its own Confidential Information.

8.3 Company's Obligations. The Company acknowledges that it may receive confidential information of HDI relating to its technical, marketing, product and/or business affairs. All such confidential information of HDI shall be-held in strict confidence by the Company and shall not be disclosed or used without express written consent of HDI, except as may be required by law. The Company shall use reasonable measures and reasonable efforts to provide protection for such confidential information of HDI, including measures at least as strict as those the Company uses to protect its own Confidential Information.
9. Warranties.

(a) Each Party represents and warrants to the other Party that (1) it is a corporation organized, validly existing and in goodstanding under the laws of the state of its incorporation; (2) it has the full right power and authority to enter into, and to perform the obligations contemplated in this Agreement, and the person signing on its behalf has the full right,

power and authority to enter into this Agreement on behalf of the Party; (3) this Agreement constitutes a legal valid and binding obligation of the Party, enforceable in accordance with its terms; and (4) the execution of this Agreement will not conflict in any way with any pre-existing agreements or understandings of the Party with any person or entity.

(b) HDI acknowledges that the Company is currently a party to a web-hosting agreement with Globix Corporation (the "Globix Agreement") for the Company's web site offering Deerskin Products to Internet customers. HDI agrees that the Company shall not be deemed in breach of any provision of this Agreement by virtue of the Globix Agreement remaining in effect after this Agreement has been executed by both Parties, provided, that the Globix Agreement is terminated on or prior to the Effective Date
10. General Provisions.

10.1 Notices. Any notice under this Agreement will be in writing and delivered by personal delivery, express courier, confirmed facsimile, or certified or registered mail, return receipt requested and will be deemed given upon personal delivery, one (1) day after deposit with express courier, upon confirmation of receipt of facsimile or five (5),days after deposit in the mail. Notices will be sent to a Party at its address set forth above or such other address as that Party may specify in writing pursuant to this Section.

10.2 No Joint Venture. The Parties agree that and acknowledge that the relationship of the Parties is in the nature of an independent contractor. This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative. Neither Party shall have any right, power or authority to enter into any agreement for or on behalf of, or to assume or create any obligation, liability, or responsibility on behalf of the other.

This Agreement will not be construed to create or imply an association, joint venture, co-ownership, or partnership between the Parties or to impose any partnership obligation or liability upon either Party.

10.3 Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon, and shall inure to the benefit of and be enforceable by, the parties hereto and their respective legal representatives, successors and assigns, but no other person shall acquire or have any rights under this Agreement.

10.4 Waiver of Breach. The failure of either Party at any time to enforce any of the provisions of this Agreement shall not be deemed or construed to be a waiver of any such provisions, or in any way to affect the right of any Party hereto to thereafter enforce each and every provision of this Agreement. No waiver of any breach of any provisions of this Agreement shall be effective unless set forth in writing and executed by the Party against which enforcement of such waiver is sought; and no waiver of any such breach shall be construed or deemed to be a waiver of any other or subsequent breach.

10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
10.6 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is declared invalid or otherwise determined to be unenforceable
for any reason, such provision shall be deemed to be severable from the remaining provisions of this Agreement, which shall otherwise remain in full force and effect.
10.7 Survival. Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

10.7 Entire Agreement. This Agreement is the complete and exclusive agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof, superseding any prior agreements and communications (both written and oral) regarding such subject matter. This Agreement may only be modified, or any rights under it waived, by a written document executed by both Parties.

10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement. This Agreement is being executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original but all of which shall constitute one and the same instrument.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have duly executed this Agreement as of the date first above written.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only audit/inspection right binding us (the Company). It already satisfies several preferred parameters: 30 days' prior written notice, exercise during our normal business hours, HDI bears the inspection cost, and scope limited to records related to payment calculations. It deviates because there is no frequency limit (unlimited inspections), no express confidentiality/independent-auditor requirement for the inspecting party, and no restriction on access to our systems or facilities. The redline adds a once-per-twelve-month cap, confines the review to copies of records that may be provided off-site, bars access to our systems, networks and facilities, and confirms confidentiality treatment (leveraging the existing Section 8 obligations), leaving the acceptable notice, business-hours and cost terms intact.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding: deviation (Section 3.4, paragraph p0022) — redline validated and submitted.**

What I found:
- The only inspection right binding us is Section 3.4, allowing HDI's General Manager to inspect the Company's records relating to payment calculations.
- Compliant elements already present: 30 days' prior written notice, exercise during our normal business hours, HDI bears inspection fees, and a narrow scope (records related to payment calculations only).
- Gaps against the preferred position: no frequency cap (unlimited inspections), no express independent-auditor/confidentiality requirement for the inspecting party, and no bar on access to our systems or facilities. Section 8.2 does bind HDI generally as to Company Confidential Information, so the confidentiality fix was a light cross-reference rather than a new regime.

Redline: added a once-per-twelve-month cap, limited the exercise to review of copies (which we may provide off-site), barred access to our systems, networks and facilities, tied the inspecting party to Section 8 confidentiality, and confirmed disclosed information is our Confidential Information — leaving the acceptable notice, business-hours and cost terms untouched. Fallback flagged in the comment (one inspection per year on 15 days' notice) if HDI pushes back.
Let me check the surrounding bargain — including HDI's development obligations and the early termination right in p0011 — to judge whether deletion or a cap is proportionate.

input.summary: Convert the Section 4.2 Termination Payment from a penalty into a cost true-up and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's non-performance.
input.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we pay only for services actually received, with no take-or-pay style charge for exiting. Section 4.2 would require us to pay HDI half of our own trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 purely for exercising our termination right, so we have limited it to a true-up of HDI's documented unrecovered Site costs and excluded terminations caused by HDI's breach or failure to launch under Section 1.6.

ops.oldText: In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: In the event the Company terminates this Agreement other than as a result of HDI's breach or failure to perform (including any failure described in Section 1.6), the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two, and (ii) HDI's documented costs actually incurred in the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and management of the Site and not recovered through payments made by the Company under Section 3 as of the Termination Date.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.context: Revenue-share hosting agreement; no minimum purchase commitment, but Section 4.2 imposes a Termination Payment on the Company equal to (trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000)/2 if the Company terminates.

input.summary: Convert the Section 4.2 Termination Payment from a penalty into a cost true-up and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's non-performance.
input.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we pay only for services actually received, with no take-or-pay style charge for exiting. Section 4.2 would require us to pay HDI half of our own trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 purely for exercising our termination right, so we have limited it to a true-up of HDI's documented unrecovered Site costs and excluded terminations caused by HDI's breach or failure to launch under Section 1.6.

ops.oldText: In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
ops.newText: In the event the Company terminates this Agreement other than as a result of HDI's breach or failure to perform (including any failure described in Section 1.6), the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two, and (ii) HDI's documented costs actually incurred in the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and management of the Site and not recovered through payments made by the Company under Section 3 as of the Termination Date.

input.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no insurance requirement even though HDI hosts the Site and handles customer orders and user data, so we have added a standard coverage covenant (general liability, errors and omissions, cyber liability and statutory workers' compensation) with certificates on request. ops.text: 10.9 Insurance. HDI shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000; (c) cyber liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000 covering HDI's processing of Confidential Information, Content and customer or user data; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. HDI shall provide the Company with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.

Comment prefix: [Playbook].

ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing

Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.

No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.

Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.summary: Insert new Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six months of transition assistance and to return, then delete and certify deletion of, Company Content and customer/order data.
input.comment: [Playbook] We have added a wind-down provision because the Agreement is silent on exit: HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, customer and order data, but has no obligation to help us migrate or to return that data on termination. Consistent with our playbook, this gives us up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification thereafter; we can discuss a ninety (90) day assistance period if the six-month tail is a concern.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site and the Company's data to the Company or its designee, for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days following the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer and order data and other data of the Company in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert new Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six months of transition assistance and to return, then delete and certify deletion of, Company Content and customer/order data.
input.comment: [Playbook] We have added a wind-down provision because the Agreement is silent on exit: HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, customer and order data, but has no obligation to help us migrate or to return that data on termination. Consistent with our playbook, this gives us up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification thereafter; we can discuss a ninety (90) day assistance period if the six-month tail is a concern.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site and the Company's data to the Company or its designee, for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days following the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer and order data and other data of the Company in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: There is no minimum purchase commitment or volume cap on us: Section 3.1 charges HDI's 30% share only on actual Net Sales above $11,000 per month, and Section 6.1 is an exclusivity (not volume) restriction. However, Section 4.2(a) attaches a penalty to our only exit route: the one-year term auto-renews annually (Section 4.1) and if the Company gives the 90-day termination notice it must pay HDI half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly installments, for services it will never receive. That is a take-or-pay style charge on exit rather than a true-up, contrary to our position that fees are payable for usage or services actually delivered. Because HDI bears all design, hosting and promotion costs (Sections 1.2, 1.6, 1.8), outright deletion is disproportionate, so we take the fallback: cap the payment at HDI's documented unrecovered Site costs (a true-up) and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's breach or failure to launch under Section 1.6.

proposal.summary: Convert the Section 4.2 Termination Payment from a penalty into a cost true-up and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's non-performance.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we pay only for services actually received, with no take-or-pay style charge for exiting. Section 4.2 would require us to pay HDI half of our own trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 purely for exercising our termination right, so we have limited it to a true-up of HDI's documented unrecovered Site costs and excluded terminations caused by HDI's breach or failure to launch under Section 1.6.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: There is no minimum purchase commitment or volume cap on us: Section 3.1 charges HDI's 30% share only on actual Net Sales above $11,000 per month, and Section 6.1 is an exclusivity (not volume) restriction. However, Section 4.2(a) attaches a penalty to our only exit route: the one-year term auto-renews annually (Section 4.1) and if the Company gives the 90-day termination notice it must pay HDI half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly installments, for services it will never receive. That is a take-or-pay style charge on exit rather than a true-up, contrary to our position that fees are payable for usage or services actually delivered. Because HDI bears all design, hosting and promotion costs (Sections 1.2, 1.6, 1.8), outright deletion is disproportionate, so we take the fallback: cap the payment at HDI's documented unrecovered Site costs (a true-up) and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's breach or failure to launch under Section 1.6.

input.quote: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement.
input.rationale: No insurance provision appears anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "insurance" and "indemn" return nothing, and Section 10 General Provisions ends at 10.8 Headings; Counterparts). HDI is a hosting/services vendor: it stores and operates the Site on its systems (1.4), processes customer orders and export files (1.5, 2.2), and has access to Content, user information and data (8.1). Under the playbook this warrants standard vendor coverage, so we insert a new Section 10.9 requiring CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M, cyber liability of USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request. Placed in the general provisions section, which also survives termination for two years under 10.7. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp) as new Section 10.9
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no insurance requirement even though HDI hosts the Site and handles customer orders and user data, so we have added a standard coverage covenant (general liability, errors and omissions, cyber liability and statutory workers' compensation) with certificates on request. input.quote: 9. Warranties.
input.rationale: Section 9 ("Warranties") contains only mutual corporate existence/authority representations (p0056-p0057) and a Globix-specific acknowledgement (p0058). Nothing in Sections 1, 5 or 9 obliges HDI to perform the design, development, hosting and maintenance services in a workmanlike manner, to have the Site conform to agreed specifications for any period, to comply with applicable law, or to keep the Site free of malicious code, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy exists. There is also no warranty disclaimer, so inserting an express warranty is a clean addition. Per the playbook this absence is a deviation requiring insertion, so we added a new Section 9(c) with a 12-month Site conformance period and a re-perform/repair/refund remedy, flagging the 90-day fallback.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 9. Warranties.
input.rationale: Section 9 ("Warranties") contains only mutual corporate existence/authority representations (p0056-p0057) and a Globix-specific acknowledgement (p0058). Nothing in Sections 1, 5 or 9 obliges HDI to perform the design, development, hosting and maintenance services in a workmanlike manner, to have the Site conform to agreed specifications for any period, to comply with applicable law, or to keep the Site free of malicious code, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy exists. There is also no warranty disclaimer, so inserting an express warranty is a clean addition. Per the playbook this absence is a deviation requiring insertion, so we added a new Section 9(c) with a 12-month Site conformance period and a re-perform/repair/refund remedy, flagging the 90-day fallback.

input.rationale: Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment (p0024-p0029), and no other provision addresses exit. HDI hosts the Site on its own server (p0007) and holds our Content, user information and data (p0009, p0016, p0048), yet there is no obligation to provide transition or migration assistance, to return that Content and customer/order data on termination, or to delete it and certify deletion. Section 10.7 survival (p0068) covers Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 only and does not cure the gap. This is the playbook's missing-transition scenario in a hosting agreement, so we insert a new Section 4.3 in the termination section reflecting the preferred position (six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within thirty days in machine-readable format, deletion plus written certification), with the 90-day fallback available.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a wind-down provision because the Agreement is silent on exit: HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, customer and order data, but has no obligation to help us migrate or to return that data on termination. Consistent with our playbook, this gives us up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification thereafter; we can discuss a ninety (90) day assistance period if the six-month tail is a concern.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site and the Company's data to the Company or its designee, for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days following the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer and order data and other data of the Company in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

payload.rationale: Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment (p0024-p0029), and no other provision addresses exit. HDI hosts the Site on its own server (p0007) and holds our Content, user information and data (p0009, p0016, p0048), yet there is no obligation to provide transition or migration assistance, to return that Content and customer/order data on termination, or to delete it and certify deletion. Section 10.7 survival (p0068) covers Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 only and does not cure the gap. This is the playbook's missing-transition scenario in a hosting agreement, so we insert a new Section 4.3 in the termination section reflecting the preferred position (six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within thirty days in machine-readable format, deletion plus written certification), with the 90-day fallback available.

Parties: we represent The Deerskin Companies, Inc.; counterparty is Hanover Direct, Inc. (HDI).

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (medium, confidence 0.62)**

**What I checked**
- Read the full agreement (all four substantive sections) rather than relying on the planner's "likely absent" hint.
- **Section 3.1 (p0019)** — fees are 30% of Net Sales *above* $11,000/month: purely usage-based, no minimum spend, no volume cap. Compliant on its face.
- **Section 6.1 (p0037)** — a restriction on us, but exclusivity/field-of-use, not a volume or purchase commitment; out of scope for this rule.
- **Sections 1.2, 1.6, 1.8** — HDI bears all development, hosting and promotion costs; commitments running *to* us, not flagged.

**The issue — Section 4.2(a) (p0026)**
The term auto-renews annually (§4.1), and our only exit (90 days' notice) triggers a "Termination Payment" of half of our own trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, payable in eight quarterly installments for services we will never receive. That is a take-or-pay-flavoured penalty on exit rather than a true-up — the precise economics the rule guards against ("we do not take-or-pay without an exit"; "replace shortfall penalties with a true-up").

**Redline (validated ok:true) — fallback level**
Given HDI genuinely funds the build and hosting, deletion would be disproportionate, so I made two minimal insertions into §4.2(a):
1. No Termination Payment where we terminate for HDI's breach or failure to launch under §1.6; and
2. The payment is capped at HDI's documented Site costs not already recovered through our §3 payments — converting the penalty into a cost true-up.

Note for the deal team: an adjacent termination-fee rule may also want to look at §4.2(c)'s eight-quarter installment tail.

content.text:
**Finding: Missing — vendor insurance (INSURANCE, severity low)**

The Agreement has no insurance provision at all. Searches for "insurance" and "indemn" return zero hits, and Section 10 (General Provisions) runs only through 10.8 (Headings; Counterparts).

HDI is squarely a hosting/services vendor under the playbook trigger:
- §1.4 — HDI stores and operates the Site on its own computer system;
- §1.5 / §2.2 — HDI generates order export/import files and processes customer orders;
- §8.1 — HDI has access to Content, user information and data of the Company.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new Section 10.9 inserted after p0070, requiring HDI to carry CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, cyber liability of USD 5M covering its processing of Confidential Information, Content and customer/user data, and statutory workers' compensation, for the term plus one year, with certificates on request. Placement in Section 10 also picks up the two-year survival in §10.7.

The comment flags our fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) in case HDI pushes back on the cyber limit.

**Finding: missing (deviation by omission) — Section 9, Warranties**

The agreement's only "Warranties" section is limited to mutual corporate existence, authority, enforceability and no-conflict representations (¶p0056–p0057), plus a Globix-specific acknowledgement (¶p0058). HDI — which designs, develops, implements, operates, maintains, manages and hosts the Site (§§1.1–1.8) — gives **no performance warranty at all**: no workmanlike-manner standard, no conformance to specifications for any period, no compliance-with-law warranty, no malicious-code warranty, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy. The Company's only protections are the §1.6 go-live termination right and the §5.2 acceptance right, neither of which survives acceptance.

Helpfully, there is also **no warranty disclaimer** anywhere in the document (no "AS IS" language), so the express warranty can be inserted cleanly without carving it out of a disclaimer.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new Section 9(c) inserted after ¶p0058 covering (1) professional and workmanlike performance consistent with industry standards, (2) Site conformance to agreed specifications for twelve (12) months following written acceptance under §5.2, (3) compliance with applicable law, and (4) no virus/malicious code — with a remedy of re-performance, repair or replacement at HDI's option and a fee refund if HDI fails to cure within thirty (30) days. A belt-and-braces sentence preserves the warranty against any future disclaimer. Note that §10.7 already lists Section 9 as surviving for two years, so the new warranty inherits survival automatically.

**Negotiation posture:** 90 days' conformance is offered as the fallback in the comment if HDI resists the 12-month period.

input.rationale: Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment (p0024-p0029), and no other provision addresses exit. HDI hosts the Site on its own server (p0007) and holds our Content, user information and data (p0009, p0016, p0048), yet there is no obligation to provide transition or migration assistance, to return that Content and customer/order data on termination, or to delete it and certify deletion. Section 10.7 survival (p0068) covers Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 only and does not cure the gap. This is the playbook's missing-transition scenario in a hosting agreement, so we insert a new Section 4.3 in the termination section reflecting the preferred position (six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within thirty days in machine-readable format, deletion plus written certification), with the 90-day fallback available.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale:
Section 4.2 imposes a stipulated sum payable by the Company (our client, the customer) to HDI, so the rule is engaged in the flagged direction. The planner hint of "likelyAbsent" was incorrect: although the document uses no "liquidated damages" label, the Termination Payment is functionally a Customer-payable liquidated amount.

It breaches the preferred position (no LD or penalty payable by Customer) and reaches the walk-away threshold on quantum. Fees under Section 3.1 are 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, whereas the Termination Payment is 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — a bill that exceeds a full year of actual fees (e.g. at $2m Net Sales: fees ~$560k/yr versus a ~$600k termination payment), and so exceeds remaining contract value. It is also triggered by any Company termination, including ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice under Section 4.1 and termination for HDI's own breach (only the narrow Section 1.6 late-launch right is expressly "without penalty"). The arrangement is one-way: Section 4.1 lets HDI walk on the same 90 days' notice for nothing, and p0028 confirms HDI never pays the Company.

I proposed the fallback rather than outright deletion because Section 1.2 has HDI bearing all Site design, development, hosting and promotion costs, recouping only through the revenue share, so some early-termination compensation is part of the genuine bargain and pure deletion would be disproportionate. The redline therefore caps the payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees, makes it the sole monetary remedy, and disapplies it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6.

input.rationale:
Section 4.2 imposes a stipulated sum payable by the Company (our client, the customer) to HDI, so the rule is engaged in the flagged direction. The planner hint of "likelyAbsent" was incorrect: although the document uses no "liquidated damages" label, the Termination Payment is functionally a Customer-payable liquidated amount.

It breaches the preferred position (no LD or penalty payable by Customer) and reaches the walk-away threshold on quantum. Fees under Section 3.1 are 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, whereas the Termination Payment is 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — a bill that exceeds a full year of actual fees (e.g. at $2m Net Sales: fees ~$560k/yr versus a ~$600k termination payment), and so exceeds remaining contract value. It is also triggered by any Company termination, including ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice under Section 4.1 and termination for HDI's own breach (only the narrow Section 1.6 late-launch right is expressly "without penalty"). The arrangement is one-way: Section 4.1 lets HDI walk on the same 90 days' notice for nothing, and p0028 confirms HDI never pays the Company.

I proposed the fallback rather than outright deletion because Section 1.2 has HDI bearing all Site design, development, hosting and promotion costs, recouping only through the revenue share, so some early-termination compensation is part of the genuine bargain and pure deletion would be disproportionate. The redline therefore caps the payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees, makes it the sole monetary remedy, and disapplies it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: MISSING (medium severity, transition)**

**Gap.** Section 4 (p0024–p0029) covers only term, 90-day termination notice and the Termination Payment. Nothing in the Agreement addresses exit, even though HDI hosts the Site on its own server (§1.3), holds our Content and administers it (§1.4/2.1), and is exposed to our "Content, user information, data" as Confidential Information (§8.1). Section 8 has no return-or-destroy obligation, and the survival clause (§10.7) covers only Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10. On termination we would have no right to migration help and no right to get our site content, customer or order data back — squarely the playbook's missing-transition scenario for a hosting agreement.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** New Section 4.3 inserted after p0029, in the termination section, at the preferred position: (a) up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, including migration cooperation; (b) return of Content, user information and customer/order data within thirty (30) days in a commonly used, machine-readable format; (c) deletion thereafter with written certification; plus express survival, since §10.7 would not otherwise carry it. The 90-day assistance fallback is flagged in the comment as a trade if HDI resists the six-month tail.

I found and addressed a deviation. Summary:

**The planner hint was wrong.** It predicted no liquidated damages were visible (`likelyAbsent: true`, pointing only at the title paragraph). A search for "liquidated damages" returned nothing, but searching "terminat" surfaced Section 4.2 — a Customer-payable stipulated sum that simply isn't labelled as liquidated damages.

**The problem (p0026).** In any Company termination, Deerskin pays HDI 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000. Cross-checking the fee clause (§3.1: 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month) shows this exceeds a full year of actual fees — at $2m Net Sales, ~$560k/yr in fees versus a ~$600k termination payment. That clears the walk-away threshold of "exceeding the remaining contract value."

Three aggravating features:
- Triggered by *any* Company termination, including ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice under §4.1 and termination for HDI's own breach (only the narrow §1.6 late-launch right is "without penalty").
- Fully one-way: §4.1 lets HDI walk on identical notice for free, and p0028 confirms HDI never pays us.
- Direction is correctly ours — the Company is our client, so this is a Customer-payable amount, not a compliant vendor-side credit.

**Why fallback rather than deletion.** §1.2 puts all Site design, development, hosting and promotion costs on HDI, recouped only through the revenue share. Some early-termination compensation is therefore part of the real bargain, making outright deletion disproportionate — and the playbook's redline guidance expressly contemplates capping an unavoidable fee at 3 months' fees. The redline caps the payment at three months' §3.1 fees, makes it the sole monetary remedy, and disapplies it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under §1.6.

One drafting note for your review: I left §4.2(b) (p0027–p0028) untouched to keep the edit minimal. Its "less than or equal to zero" mechanic still functions under the new formula but is now largely vestigial, so you may want to tidy it if the cap is accepted.

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2 — verified findings and negotiation posture

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.2. The Agreement is materially thin on customer protections and carries three critical gaps and three walk-away items.

Most significantly, the Agreement contains **no indemnification, no intellectual property or data ownership provision, and no limitation of liability**. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site, supplies the software and hosting environment, and holds our Content, customer information and Confidential Information — yet nothing vests ownership of the deliverables, Content or Site customer data in us, nothing obliges HDI to defend us against third-party IP or data-security claims, and both parties face unlimited direct and consequential liability. There is also no performance warranty, no transition assistance or data return on exit, and no vendor insurance covenant.

On the commercial terms, the risk allocation is one-sided against us. Section 6.1 imposes an open-ended exclusive-dealing and non-compete restraint on the Company across "substantially similar" products for a term that auto-renews annually, with no performance-based exit. Section 4.2 imposes a Customer-payable Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — more than a full year of actual fees under the Section 3.1 revenue share — triggered by *any* Company termination, including ordinary non-renewal and termination for HDI's own breach, while HDI may walk on the same 90 days' notice for nothing.

Fallback: HDI owns the build subject to a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free licence to us. |

Add mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with our payment obligations outside the cap. Add our affiliate/successor carve-out, require our consent (not unreasonably withheld) for HDI assignments with a competitor bar, and confirm a Company change of control is not an assignment and gives HDI no termination or re-pricing right. |

Fallback: 90 days' assistance. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Deviation | § 1.4 | No minimum purchase or volume cap (fees accrue only on actual Net Sales above $11,000/month), but §4.2(a) is a take-or-pay charge on exit payable in eight quarterly instalments for services never received. | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 1.4 | §4.1 auto-renews for one-year terms (acceptable length) but requires 90 days' non-renewal notice with no renewal reminder. | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § 1.4 | §3.4 already provides 30 days' notice, our business hours, HDI-borne cost and payment-records-only scope, but has no frequency limit, confidentiality requirement or systems-access restriction. | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 5.4 | New York law matches our position and there is no arbitration clause, but the clause omits forum selection. Add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, leaving the existing sentence intact. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 1.4 | The only most-favoured-treatment language (§1.8) runs in our favour; §3.1 has no benchmarking or price-matching mechanic and §7.1 cross-promotion is mutual. No redline proposed. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 5.4 | No personnel covenant anywhere; §5.4's appointed-representative provisions impose no hiring restraint. Already at our preferred position; no redline needed. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 5.4 | No insurance provision, despite HDI hosting the Site, processing orders and export files and accessing Content and user data. Insert new §10.9: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These three findings sit at the playbook's walk-away threshold and should be resolved before signature:

1. **No vendor IP indemnity (INDEMN, critical).** The absence of any HDI defence and indemnity — in an agreement where HDI supplies the software, technology and hosting environment and handles our Content and customer information — is the playbook walk-away position.
2. **Open-ended exclusive dealing on the Company (EXCLUSIVITY, high).** §6.1 restrains us for the full, annually auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit, matching the playbook's walk-away pattern. We propose the fallback (Deerskin Products, 12 months, automatic termination on HDI performance failure) given HDI's reciprocal covenants in §6.3.
3. **Customer-payable Termination Payment quantum (LD, high).** §4.2 exceeds a full year of actual fees and remaining contract value, applies to ordinary non-renewal and to termination for HDI's own breach, and is entirely one-way. We propose a three-month fee cap and disapplication on HDI breach rather than deletion, recognising that HDI funds Site development and recoups through the revenue share.

We also treat the two remaining criticals — **absent IP/data ownership** and **absent limitation of liability** — as must-fix. We should not sign an agreement in which a vendor hosts our customer data with no ownership provision and unlimited exposure on both sides.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** implementing the proposals above, sequenced so that the three criticals (indemnity in §9, ownership in new §5.5, liability cap as §9(c)) and the three walk-away items lead the cover note.
2. **Confirm the commercial baseline** with the business team: trailing Net Sales and monthly run-rate, so we can quantify the §4.2 exposure and pressure-test the three-month fee cap and the USD 1,000,000 liability floor.
3. **Agree the fallback ladder internally** before the first call: 12-month/Deerskin-only exclusivity; three-month cap (or cost true-up) on the Termination Payment; HDI-owned build with a perpetual royalty-free licence; 90-day transition assistance; 60-day non-renewal window; E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.
4. **Ask HDI two diligence questions:** the hosting and data-security arrangements (including the Globix relationship referenced in §9) and its current insurance certificates, to support the new §10.9 covenant.
5. **Preserve drafting placement** — indemnity, warranty and cap inside §9 and the transition clause as new §4.3 — to avoid renumbering and to capture the existing §10.7 survival.
6. **No action** on MFN (§1.8) or non-solicitation; both are already at our preferred position."}
